Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving its implementing regulation; Law 18/2022 of 28 September implementing EU Directive 2018/843 and strengthening beneficial-owner transparency; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Registry of Beneficial Ownership (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales); Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July approving the Spanish Companies Act; Law 10/2010 and Royal Decree 304/2014 require identification and verification of the beneficial owner by obliged entities.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A registered office in Spain is mandatory under the Spanish Companies Act and must be a real address where company administration and management are located or where the principal establishment or operation is situated. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable for a passive holding company if the provider contractually permits registered-office use, receives official notices, maintains reliable records, and permits access for inspections. It is not sufficient where the address is merely a mail drop, where management is conducted elsewhere, or where banking, tax, transfer-pricing, treaty-benefit, or economic-substance requirements require actual Spanish activity. A holding company should maintain Spanish corporate books, board and shareholder records, accounting, bank evidence, decision-making records, and demonstrable governance substance.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is situated (e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid), under the Directorate General for Legal Certainty and Public Faith, Ministry of the Presidency, Justice and Relations with the Cortes. The corporate name index is reserved through the Registro Mercantil Central.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, approving the consolidated text of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC). Core provisions: Article 4 (minimum capital), Articles 20-24 (formation by public deed and registration), Article 26 (name reservation), Article 62 (deposit of capital and bank certificate), Articles 67-68 (expert valuation of non-cash contributions), Article 79 (full subscription and payment for the SL), and Article 209 (managing powers). Complemented by the Mercantile Registry Regulations (Royal Decree 1784/1996) and Royal Decree 609/2023 (register of ultimate beneficial owners).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura Pública de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) executed before a Spanish notary, filed electronically or in person with the Provincial Mercantile Registry and recorded as the company's first inscription (hoja de inscripción).

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 43 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

The SL requires a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000 (LSC Article 4(1)), fully subscribed and fully paid in cash at the time of incorporation (LSC Article 79). The capital must be deposited with an authorized credit institution in the company's incorporation account and evidenced by a bank deposit certificate (LSC Article 62). The depositary bank may not release the funds until the mercantile registration is credited, or until two months have elapsed from the date of the certificate without registration. Non-cash contributions require an independent expert valuation report. Formal escrow accounts are not used; the statutory bank-certificate regime operates as an equivalent restriction.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety compliance certificate (Certificado de Bomberos or technical conformity report) issued by the municipal fire service, demonstrating conformity with the CTE DB-SI fire-safety requirements, including evacuation routes, extinguishers, and emergency lighting; structural and occupancy certificate of the premises; workplace clearance under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales, including appointment of an external prevention service, initial risk assessment, health surveillance agreement, and an emergency and evacuation plan adapted to the office activity; and, where required, registration of the administrative activity with the municipal civil-protection register.

Paid-in capital rule: The SL requires a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000 (LSC Article 4(1)), fully subscribed and fully paid in cash at the time of incorporation (LSC Article 79). The capital must be deposited with an authorized credit institution in the company's incorporation account and evidenced by a bank deposit certificate (LSC Article 62). The depositary bank may not release the funds until the mercantile registration is credited, or until two months have elapsed from the date of the certificate without registration. Non-cash contributions require an independent expert valuation report. Formal escrow accounts are not used; the statutory bank-certificate regime operates as an equivalent restriction.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
WHEREAS the Founding Partners have subscribed the full share capital of EUR 3,000, divided into 3,000 equal participations of EUR 1 each, fully paid up as evidenced by the bank deposit certificate, IT IS RESOLVED: 1. To ratify the subscription and full payment of the 3,000 participations as set out in the subscription list. 2. To establish the registered office at [full Spanish address], within the territorial jurisdiction of the Provincial Mercantile Registry, where legal notices shall be served. 3. To appoint [name, ID number] as Sole Administrator, with all statutory powers of representation and management, pursuant to Article 209 of the Capital Companies Act. This resolution is attached to the public deed of incorporation and filed for mercantile registration.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Dirección General de Industria of the competent Autonomous Community (in Madrid: Dirección General de Industria, Energía y Minas, Consejería de Economía, Hacienda y Empleo), together with the municipal licensing office (Área de Licencias) of the Ayuntamiento where the registered office is located.

Category: Licencia de Apertura y Funcionamiento, or, where the applicable municipal ordinance so provides, a Declaración Responsable de Apertura filed by the company for the occupation of office premises as the registered office and administrative seat of a passive equity holding company.

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Spanish Tax Agency, official portal: https://www.agenciatributaria.gob.es/

E-government filing portal

Spanish resident entities such as SL obtain NIF (CIF) upon incorporation through the Registro Mercantil Central. Non-resident owners may require separate registration with AEAT for tax purposes if conducting business in Spain; procedure involves submitting incorporation documents, articles of association, and tax identification via the AEAT online portal or in-person at tax offices.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — Spanish resident entities such as SL obtain NIF (CIF) upon incorporation through the Registro Mercantil Central. Non-resident owners may require separate registration with AEAT for tax purposes if conducting business in Spain; procedure involves submitting incorporation documents, articles of association, and tax identification via the AEAT online portal or in-person at tax offices.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

No US-style check-the-box elections available in Spain. Spanish companies are subject to entity-level taxation under the Impuesto sobre Sociedades. Limited hybrid mismatch relief or specific holding company regimes may apply under certain conditions, but no general election mechanisms.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

50,000 EUR annual turnover threshold for VAT registration

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

VAT zero-rated on goods exported outside the EU upon proof of export. Offshore services may qualify for zero-rating or reverse charge depending on destination. Criteria include valid customs export declaration and proof of non-EU destination.

  • Customs Export Declaration (Despacho de Exportación)
  • Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment

Mandatory facturación electrónica for B2B sales via AEAT platform. Large taxpayers must comply with real-time invoicing and digital stamping requirements; API integrations for electronic clearance in certain sectors.

AEAT audits can lead to retrospective denial of zero-rating, clawback of VAT credits, penalties up to 100% of evaded amounts, and criminal sanctions for fraudulent claims.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain uses the euro and has no general exchange-control regime or restriction on conversion between euros and foreign currencies for ordinary commercial, investment, dividend, or financing transactions. Current-account payments, including dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, trade payments, and intercompany settlements, are generally freely transferable, subject to tax, anti-money-laundering, sanctions, transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, and documentary requirements. Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment, acquisitions, shareholder loans, capital contributions, and repatriation of investment proceeds, are generally permitted without prior exchange-control approval, but may trigger investment declarations, statistical reporting, foreign-asset reporting, or sector-specific screening. Profit remittance by a Spanish SL is subject to distributable-profit tests, maintenance of legally required reserves, solvency and corporate-law requirements, withholding-tax analysis, applicable treaty relief, beneficial-owner documentation, and evidence that the payment is a genuine dividend or arm's-length financing return. Banks may require board or shareholder resolutions, audited or approved accounts, tax residence certificates, ownership-chain records, and source-of-funds evidence before processing material transfers.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain has no statutory mandatory surrender requirement and no prescribed mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Export receipts may generally remain in euros or foreign currencies and may be held in domestic or foreign accounts, subject to accurate accounting, tax reporting, bank compliance, sanctions screening, and applicable statistical declarations. There is no general statutory deadline requiring conversion or repatriation of export proceeds. Transactions with non-residents may be reportable through Banco de España statistical reporting mechanisms, generally based on information supplied by resident payment service providers and financial institutions; direct reporting obligations may arise where transactions are not captured by reporting intermediaries or where applicable foreign-asset and investment declarations are triggered. Cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more when entering or leaving the European Union, and domestic movements subject to applicable Spanish rules, require the prescribed declaration. Any export business operated by the holding company should separately assess customs, VAT, Intrastat, transfer-pricing, and trade-sanctions obligations.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; applicable foreign-exchange reporting and statistical obligations are supplemented by the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise and the Directorate-General of Trade Policy.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium for payment operations and low-to-medium as a substitute for a Spanish relationship bank. An EU-authorised electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, safeguarded funds, SEPA transfers, international payments, and, where separately authorised, foreign-exchange services. It generally cannot accept repayable deposits as a bank, provide unrestricted banking credit, or automatically provide a Spanish corporate bank account. An offshore digital EMI without EU passporting, Spanish establishment, or a regulated EEA service provider is unsuitable as the primary account for a Spanish SL. Availability may be restricted for holding companies, financial flows involving multiple jurisdictions, shareholder loans, dividend concentration, nominee arrangements, high-risk countries, or transactions lacking an identifiable commercial purpose. The company must verify the institution's authorisation in the relevant EBA or national register, safeguarding model, IBAN country, access to SEPA and SWIFT, sanctions controls, transaction limits, account-closure rights, and data-retention procedures.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Passive holding company with no operating revenue, employees, or clearly documented investment rationale.

Root cause: Passive holding company with no operating revenue, employees, or clearly documented investment rationale.

Defense evidence: Business memorandum describing the intermediate holding function; group organisational chart; investment policy; target subsidiary profiles; board-approved treasury policy; projected cash flows; expected payment corridors; shareholder and financing agreements; financial model; explanation of substance, directors, accounting support, and decision-making in Spain.
Non-resident ownership, layered entities, trusts, nominee shareholders, or difficulty identifying the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner.

Root cause: Non-resident ownership, layered entities, trusts, nominee shareholders, or difficulty identifying the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner.

Defense evidence: Certified constitutional documents for every ownership layer; current commercial-register extracts; shareholder registers; ownership chart to each natural-person beneficial owner; passports and proof of address; trust or foundation instruments where relevant; declarations of control; notarised, apostilled, translated, and dated documents where requested.
Incoming capital contribution or shareholder loan from an offshore entity or a jurisdiction viewed as higher risk.

Root cause: Incoming capital contribution or shareholder loan from an offshore entity or a jurisdiction viewed as higher risk.

Defense evidence: Executed contribution or loan agreement; corporate approvals; lender and investor KYC; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; audited accounts; bank statements; tax returns; proof of original funding; beneficial-owner evidence; purpose code and payment narrative; sanctions and adverse-media screening; repayment and interest terms demonstrating arm's-length treatment.
Large dividend, interest, royalty, or management-fee payments to related parties.

Root cause: Large dividend, interest, royalty, or management-fee payments to related parties.

Defense evidence: Approved financial statements; distributable-profit calculation; reserve analysis; shareholder resolution; intercompany agreement; transfer-pricing support; withholding-tax analysis; tax residence and beneficial-owner certificates; invoice or payment schedule; evidence of services or financing; board approval; confirmation that the recipient is not a sanctioned or restricted party.
Expected transactions involving Latin America, high-risk countries, cash-intensive businesses, virtual assets, or opaque intermediaries.

Root cause: Expected transactions involving Latin America, high-risk countries, cash-intensive businesses, virtual assets, or opaque intermediaries.

Defense evidence: Country and counterparty risk matrix; customer and supplier register; contracts, invoices, bills of lading, customs records, and purchase orders; sanctions screening protocol; beneficial-owner verification; anti-bribery policy; transaction-monitoring rules; explanation of the commercial rationale; independent compliance review; prohibition or escalation procedures for cash and virtual-asset exposure.
Mismatch between registered activity and account activity, including a holding company conducting trade, logistics, payroll, or payment-aggregation transactions.

Root cause: Mismatch between registered activity and account activity, including a holding company conducting trade, logistics, payroll, or payment-aggregation transactions.

Defense evidence: Updated corporate-purpose statement; management representation; business-plan revision; licences or registrations where applicable; intercompany service agreements; staffing and outsourcing contracts; invoices and logistics documentation; VAT and customs registrations; forecast transaction volumes; request for separate operational accounts or a separate operating subsidiary.
Use of virtual offices, nominee directors, unexplained Spanish addresses, or directors who cannot explain the group structure.

Root cause: Use of virtual offices, nominee directors, unexplained Spanish addresses, or directors who cannot explain the group structure.

Defense evidence: Lease or registered-office evidence; local administrator and director engagement letters; proof of management activities; accounting and legal-service agreements; board minutes; tax registrations; live interview preparation; role descriptions; explanation of governance, authority matrix, and location of key decisions.
Incomplete corporate documents, expired certificates, inconsistent names, untranslated records, or missing tax identification numbers.

Root cause: Incomplete corporate documents, expired certificates, inconsistent names, untranslated records, or missing tax identification numbers.

Defense evidence: Recent certified extracts from the Registro Mercantil; notarised statutes and deeds; valid NIE or NIF records; apostilled and sworn translations where required; specimen signatures; powers of attorney; incumbency certificate; tax-residence evidence; document-control checklist with consistent legal names and dates.
High-value or unusual transfers that lack a clear payment purpose or contain generic descriptions such as 'investment' or 'services'.

Root cause: High-value or unusual transfers that lack a clear payment purpose or contain generic descriptions such as 'investment' or 'services'.

Defense evidence: Pre-advice package containing the executed contract, invoice, board approval, purpose classification, counterparty KYC, source-and-use-of-funds schedule, tax treatment, expected settlement date, and supporting commercial documents. Payment narratives should accurately identify capital contribution, shareholder loan, dividend, interest, trade settlement, or other lawful purpose.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Route equity through a Spanish bank or regulated EEA payment institution capable of evidencing the remitter, beneficial owner, and purpose. Use a dedicated capital subscription or shareholder-loan account where available, with the payment narrative stating the exact legal purpose, such as 'share capital contribution pursuant to [date] resolution' or 'shareholder loan pursuant to [agreement date]'. Before receipt, provide the bank with the subscription or loan agreement, shareholder or board resolution, ownership chart, source-of-funds evidence, lender KYC, beneficial-owner documents, and expected amount and currency. For incorporation, obtain bank confirmation of the deposited amount when required by the notary or commercial-registration process; Spanish corporate-law changes may make bank certification optional in certain circumstances, but the bank and notary may still request evidence. Reconcile the incoming wire to the accounting ledger and retain records for AML, tax, corporate, and statistical reporting. Use SEPA credit transfer for euro funding within SEPA and SWIFT cross-border payment rails for non-SEPA currencies or countries. Screen all parties, banks, intermediary banks, countries, vessels, and goods against applicable EU, UN, UK, and US sanctions according to the company's risk policy.Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments and SWIFT cross-border payments for non-SEPA transactions. A SWIFT MT103 is the traditional customer credit-transfer message; banks are progressively migrating to ISO 20022 customer-credit-transfer messaging, including pacs.008, so the treasury policy should require confirmation of the bank's current format and retention of the end-to-end transaction reference. For documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit, preferably an irrevocable documentary credit subject to UCP 600, issued or advised by a regulated bank. Validate applicant, beneficiary, issuing bank, confirming bank, Incoterms, shipping documents, insurance, inspection certificates, sanctions clauses, discrepancy procedures, expiry, presentation period, and governing law. Documentary collections may use URC 522 where suitable. For open-account trade, require approved counterparties, purchase orders, invoices, delivery evidence, segregation of duties, dual approval, and payment matching. Do not use the holding company as a payment conduit for unrelated third-party trade without documented corporate purpose, appropriate registrations, and bank approval. Maintain payment files containing contracts, invoices, customs or transport documents, VAT treatment, sanctions screening, and reconciliation evidence.Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorised bank or investment firm, documented under appropriate master trading terms, with defined notional, currency pair, maturity, settlement instructions, exposure rationale, counterparty limits, valuation, collateral, and accounting treatment.Non-deliverable forwards for currencies subject to local convertibility restrictions or where the bank offers cash-settled hedging. The company should verify that the instrument is permitted for the relevant currency, is used for a genuine underlying exposure or approved treasury strategy, and satisfies MiFID II, EMIR, reporting, suitability, appropriateness, and collateral requirements applicable to the counterparties.Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for longer-term shareholder loans, acquisition financing, or recurring currency exposures, subject to bank counterparty approval, ISDA or equivalent documentation, EMIR classification and reporting, collateral terms, valuation controls, and board-approved risk limits.Foreign-exchange options and collars may be used for documented exposures where the company understands premium, exercise, settlement, early-termination, and contingent-liability risks. Written treasury-policy approval, independent valuation, and appropriate accounting documentation are required.Spot foreign-exchange transactions for settlement and liquidity management, with segregation between transactional conversion and speculative positions. Maintain exposure registers, hedge-designation records where hedge accounting is applied, counterparty limits, confirmation matching, independent valuation, and periodic board or treasury-committee reporting.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium for payment operations and low-to-medium as a substitute for a Spanish relationship bank. An EU-authorised electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, safeguarded funds, SEPA transfers, international payments, and, where separately authorised, foreign-exchange services. It generally cannot accept repayable deposits as a bank, provide unrestricted banking credit, or automatically provide a Spanish corporate bank account. An offshore digital EMI without EU passporting, Spanish establishment, or a regulated EEA service provider is unsuitable as the primary account for a Spanish SL. Availability may be restricted for holding companies, financial flows involving multiple jurisdictions, shareholder loans, dividend concentration, nominee arrangements, high-risk countries, or transactions lacking an identifiable commercial purpose. The company must verify the institution's authorisation in the relevant EBA or national register, safeguarding model, IBAN country, access to SEPA and SWIFT, sanctions controls, transaction limits, account-closure rights, and data-retention procedures.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general corporate income tax rate (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Ley 27/2014, Art. 29.1); new small companies may apply 15% for the first two profitable years only where they carry on an active economic activity, not applicable to a pure equity holding SPV.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% statutory dividend withholding tax applied to distributions made by an SL to non-resident shareholders under Art. 25.1.j of the Non-Resident Income Tax Law (IRNR); resident corporate shareholders and EU/EEA parent companies meeting the 5% shareholding threshold may obtain exemption under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, leaving a 0% effective WHT; non-qualifying foreign shareholders are subject to the 19% rate unless a DTA grants a lower rate.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal-year end; for an SL with a 31 December year-end, the filing window runs from 1 April to 25 July of the following year.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 108 – Resultado contable del ejercicio Net accounting profit or loss before corporate income tax, prepared under Spanish GAAP (Plan General Contable) and shown in the annual accounts; for the holding SL this includes gross dividend income and capital gains on disposal of subsidiary shares. The SL itself is the resident taxpayer; the foreign ultimate parent exercises no direct filing rights. The Spanish legal representative or tax agent must file; all foreign-source dividends received by the SL are reported here gross before any ETVE exemption adjustment. Late filing without prior AEAT notice triggers the extemporaneous surcharge (recargo extemporáneo, Art. 27 LGT): 5% of net tax due if filed within the first 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (4% to 5% annual). Incorrect or understated returns that produce an assessed tax deficiency carry a proportional sanction under Art. 191 LGT of 50% to 150% of the unduly unpaid amount, reduced to 30% to 60% upon conformity; deliberate concealment through shell structures increases the penalty range; refusal to file at all after AEAT notification carries a flat penalty of EUR 1,000 plus 20% of the assessed amount in the most severe cases.
Box 110 – Ajustes al resultado contable (diferencias permanentes) Permanent differences between accounting result and taxable base; the ETVE participation exemption adjustment is made here, removing qualifying exempt dividends and capital gains from the tax base. Retain the foreign subsidiary's tax residence certificate, holding-period evidence and comparable-tax statement; non-resident shareholders must provide their own TRC to support treaty relief only at the distribution stage, not on this CIT return. Late filing without prior AEAT notice triggers the extemporaneous surcharge (recargo extemporáneo, Art. 27 LGT): 5% of net tax due if filed within the first 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (4% to 5% annual). Incorrect or understated returns that produce an assessed tax deficiency carry a proportional sanction under Art. 191 LGT of 50% to 150% of the unduly unpaid amount, reduced to 30% to 60% upon conformity; deliberate concealment through shell structures increases the penalty range; refusal to file at all after AEAT notification carries a flat penalty of EUR 1,000 plus 20% of the assessed amount in the most severe cases.
Box 155 – Base imponible antes de compensación Gross taxable base after accounting adjustments and before applying prior-year negative taxable bases; for an ETVE-qualified SL this base is zero where the only income is exempt participation income. Verify that the SPV's income sources are strictly passive dividends and capital gains; any management, financing, or service revenue would taint the ETVE status and expose the SPV to the standard 25% rate and TP adjustments. Late filing without prior AEAT notice triggers the extemporaneous surcharge (recargo extemporáneo, Art. 27 LGT): 5% of net tax due if filed within the first 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (4% to 5% annual). Incorrect or understated returns that produce an assessed tax deficiency carry a proportional sanction under Art. 191 LGT of 50% to 150% of the unduly unpaid amount, reduced to 30% to 60% upon conformity; deliberate concealment through shell structures increases the penalty range; refusal to file at all after AEAT notification carries a flat penalty of EUR 1,000 plus 20% of the assessed amount in the most severe cases.
Box 156 – Compensación de bases imponibles negativas Set-off of prior-year tax losses; Spain permits indefinite carry-forward but applies annual offset caps of 50% to 70% of the current tax base depending on net turnover (Art. 26 LIS). Holding SPVs that recorded impairment losses on foreign subsidiaries must keep full computation schedules; AEAT may challenge loss utilisation where the SPV lacked economic activity and was artificially inserted between the foreign parent and the operating subsidiary. Late filing without prior AEAT notice triggers the extemporaneous surcharge (recargo extemporáneo, Art. 27 LGT): 5% of net tax due if filed within the first 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (4% to 5% annual). Incorrect or understated returns that produce an assessed tax deficiency carry a proportional sanction under Art. 191 LGT of 50% to 150% of the unduly unpaid amount, reduced to 30% to 60% upon conformity; deliberate concealment through shell structures increases the penalty range; refusal to file at all after AEAT notification carries a flat penalty of EUR 1,000 plus 20% of the assessed amount in the most severe cases.
Box 169 – Cuota íntegra Total gross CIT liability computed as the adjusted tax base multiplied by 25% before tax credits, exemptions and double-taxation relief. For a fully ETVE-exempt holding SL this box is zero; if any non-exempt income remains, the quota must reflect the 25% rate and no reduction may be claimed for foreign withholding taxes except through the international double-taxation credit formalities. Late filing without prior AEAT notice triggers the extemporaneous surcharge (recargo extemporáneo, Art. 27 LGT): 5% of net tax due if filed within the first 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (4% to 5% annual). Incorrect or understated returns that produce an assessed tax deficiency carry a proportional sanction under Art. 191 LGT of 50% to 150% of the unduly unpaid amount, reduced to 30% to 60% upon conformity; deliberate concealment through shell structures increases the penalty range; refusal to file at all after AEAT notification carries a flat penalty of EUR 1,000 plus 20% of the assessed amount in the most severe cases.
Box 171 – Bonificaciones, deducciones, retenciones e ingresos a cuenta Tax credits applied against the full quota, including international double-taxation credits (Art. 31 LIS), withholdings suffered at source, the ETVE exemption adjustment and quarterly advance payments. Foreign withholding taxes suffered by the SL on inbound dividends are creditable here only where the ETVE exemption is inapplicable; foreign shareholders cannot claim these Spanish credits on this form and must use Modelo 210 for treaty refunds. Late filing without prior AEAT notice triggers the extemporaneous surcharge (recargo extemporáneo, Art. 27 LGT): 5% of net tax due if filed within the first 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (4% to 5% annual). Incorrect or understated returns that produce an assessed tax deficiency carry a proportional sanction under Art. 191 LGT of 50% to 150% of the unduly unpaid amount, reduced to 30% to 60% upon conformity; deliberate concealment through shell structures increases the penalty range; refusal to file at all after AEAT notification carries a flat penalty of EUR 1,000 plus 20% of the assessed amount in the most severe cases.
Box 200 – Cuota diferencial (resultado de la liquidación) Final tax payable or refundable after deducting quarterly prepayments (Modelo 202) and source withholdings; this is the balance due with the Modelo 200. Any positive balance must be paid via the AEAT debit mandate or card by the statutory deadline; refunds are remitted to the SL's Spanish bank account within six months. Foreign parent lenders must not cause the SL to waive refunds outstanding in favour of intercompany loans, as this triggers a deemed advance distribution and 19% withholding. Late filing without prior AEAT notice triggers the extemporaneous surcharge (recargo extemporáneo, Art. 27 LGT): 5% of net tax due if filed within the first 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest (4% to 5% annual). Incorrect or understated returns that produce an assessed tax deficiency carry a proportional sanction under Art. 191 LGT of 50% to 150% of the unduly unpaid amount, reduced to 30% to 60% upon conformity; deliberate concealment through shell structures increases the penalty range; refusal to file at all after AEAT notification carries a flat penalty of EUR 1,000 plus 20% of the assessed amount in the most severe cases.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 250,000 – mandatory Local File (expediente del contribuyente) is required when the aggregate annual value of related-party transactions reaches or exceeds EUR 250,000, or when the taxpayer's net turnover exceeds EUR 10 million even below that transaction threshold; Master File (documentación del grupo) is additionally mandatory for members of a consolidated group whose global consolidated turnover is at least EUR 20 million; Country-by-Country Report is triggered where the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue equals or exceeds EUR 750 million.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a standalone ESR code; economic substance is instead enforced under the ETVE requirements (substantial means: real directorship, management involvement in the foreign subsidiaries, accounting records in Spain, qualified personnel proportionate to the portfolio), the general anti-abuse rule (Art. 15 LIS – conflicto en la aplicación de la norma tributaria), the simulation doctrine (Art. 13 LGT) recharacterising artificial holding arrangements, the CFC rules (Art. 100 LIS) taxing passive income of controlled foreign entities in low-tax jurisdictions, and the EU abuse-of-rights jurisprudence: a pure equity holding SPV that lacks personnel, premises and decision-making substance may be denied ETVE exemption, treaty benefits and Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Conduct (Defraudación Tributaria)

Statutory sanction: Criminal offense under Art. 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code: imprisonment from 1 to 5 years plus a fine of up to 6 times the defrauded quota (multa de tantas al séxtuplo) where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000; aggravation to 2 to 6 years' imprisonment where shell corporations or instrumentality entities are used; loss of the right to obtain tax benefits, public subsidies and public procurement contracts for 4 to 7 years, publication of the judgment, and civil liability for the tax debt and interest.

Director personal liability: Directors may be declared jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt under Art. 42.2.b) LGT where they wilfully created or knowingly used a shell SPV to evade tax; criminal conviction entails international travel bans (passport withdrawal), entry bans to public procurement markets and imprisonment; dissolution of the SL does not extinguish director liability, and the veil-piercing doctrine allows AEAT to seize personal assets of the administrator.
Transfer Pricing And Artificial Substance Mispricing

Statutory sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment under Art. 18 LIS plus late-payment interest and a proportional penalty under Art. 191 LGT of 50% to 100% (up to 150% if deliberate) of the reassessed deficiency; fixed fine of EUR 1,500 for missing, incomplete or inaccurate TP documentation (Art. 18.13 LIS); reclassification of the SPV as a mere financial arrangement annulling the ETVE exemption and recharacterising dividend flows as taxable income with a 25% CIT charge and 19% WHT.

Director personal liability: Administrators who sign knowingly distorted declarations are subsidiary liable for the assessed deficiency under Art. 43.1 LGT after the insolvency of the company; AEAT may issue derivative liability assessments (derivación de responsabilidad) against directors who caused the lack of substance or authorised the artificial pricing, with direct recourse to personal bank accounts, real estate and travel controls; criminal exposure arises where the amount reassessed exceeds EUR 120,000.
AML and Beneficial-Owner Concealment (Blanqueo de Capitales)

Statutory sanction: Administrative sanction under Ley 10/2010 and Law 6/2023: very serious infractions subject to fines from EUR 150,000 to EUR 6,000,000 (or up to 10% of net turnover), serious infractions from EUR 60,001 to EUR 150,000, and minor infractions up to EUR 60,000; criminal money-laundering offense under Art. 301 of the Criminal Code: imprisonment from 6 months to 6 years, fines, forfeiture of the assets laundered and publication of the sentence.

Director personal liability: Directors, compliance officers and the ultimate beneficial owner are personally punishable for AML breaches regardless of corporate capacity, with fines imposed directly on their persons; conviction triggers travel bans, disqualification from managing companies for up to 10 years and, in cross-border laundering cases, extradition exposure; the corporate veil is pierced so that personal assets of the beneficial owner may be seized if the SPV's assets and the individual's patrimony are mixed.
